title: Targeted GPU scarcity and dependent-service silencing chaos experiment
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Objective: validate that (1) multi-region failover and routing logic keeps the platform within SLOs when a single region experiences progressive GPU pool depletion, (2) per-tenant circuit breakers trigger and isolate noisy tenants, and (3) dependent services can be selectively 'silenced' (blackholed) without causing uncontrolled error-budget burn across regions. This ticket provisions a controlled, staged experiment that combines a GPU resource drain simulator with a dependency blackhole proxy while exercising our routing and autoscale/fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled GPU depletion in region-us-west-2 reaches 70% and 95% simulated unavailability without full regional evacuation
Automatic routing shifts 20% of affected traffic to regional standby pools and compatible model variants (quantized/low-latency variants) within configured SLO window
Tenant-level circuit breakers trip for noisy tenants and recovery is observed according to our circuit policy (cooldown and half-open trial) without cascading failures
Dependency blackhole for non-critical downstream (metric-ingest service) does not cause cross-region cascading 500s; error budget burn remains under defined threshold (<=10% of 1-day budget)
Post-run incident report with root cause statement, runbook updates, and recommended config changes (batching/route weights/circuit thresholds) is published
test_plan: Stage 0 (Dry-run): run simulator in canary with 1% production traffic on staging cluster; validate observability and safety gates
Stage 1 (Targeted low-impact): inject mild GPU availability reduction (20-35%) in non-primary availability zone of us-west-2; enable dependency blackhole for metric-ingest-v2 for a 2-minute window
Stage 2 (Escalation): escalate GPU drain to 70% across pool and extend blackhole to 10 minutes; observe circuit breaker behavior and routing decisions for 30 minutes
Stage 3 (Stress): push GPU availability to 95% (simulate node OOM/eviction storm) with sustained 15-minute blackhole; validate automatic regional evacuation and tenant-level shedding
Each stage includes a fail-closed safety check: abort if p99 latency exceeds baseline by >3x for 5m or error-rate rises >12% absolute for 5m
safety_measures: Run only during maintenance window (2026-03-15 02:00–06:00 UTC) and with page-on Slack alerting enabled
Traffic quota cap: experiment limited to max 25% of production ingress for affected region and rolled back by control-plane if breached
Automated abort hooks wired to SLO guardrails (p95/p99 latency and 5xx rate thresholds) and to manual abort by SRE lead
Use synthetic tenants (tenant IDs in experiment allowlist) plus a small subset of low-risk real tenants with opt-in consent
Backup routing: immediate fallback to warm standby region and faster model variant if critical thresholds tripped
rollback_plan: Immediate abort: disable injector and blackhole proxy; restore original routing weights via control-plane rollback API
If control-plane is degraded: issue global prefix route disable and divert traffic to pre-provisioned fallback endpoints
Post-abort: run healing job to drain hot queues and clear temporary rate-limits; annotate incident in incident tracker
If tenant state corrupts: initiate data-integrity verification job and notify affected customers per incident policy
metrics_to_track: SLOs: text-generation availability (successful responses within 500ms) — daily and 1h windows
Latency: p50/p95/p99 token latency and end-to-end request latency per region
Error rates: 4xx/5xx rates per service and per tenant
Circuit metrics: circuit open/close counts, average cooldown durations, half-open success ratio
Autoscaler decisions: scale-up events, time-to-provision GPU nodes, queue length
Traffic shift: percentage of requests routed away from affected region and to compatible model variants
Error budget burn: cumulative and per-tenant during experiment window
dashboards: Tracing: Jaeger trace tag 'chaos_experiment=ENG-51799' for easy filtering
